description:
## Why

RSA-PKCS1v15 + SHA-256 is implemented (`RsaPkcs1v15Sha256Verifier` at `lib.rs:1909`). The SHA-384 and SHA-512 variants share 95% of the implementation but use different OIDs.

OIDs:
* `1.2.840.113549.1.1.12` (sha384WithRSAEncryption)
* `1.2.840.113549.1.1.13` (sha512WithRSAEncryption)

## What

In `pkix-path/src/lib.rs`, generic-ize the existing RSA verifier OR add two more unit structs (`RsaPkcs1v15Sha384Verifier`, `RsaPkcs1v15Sha512Verifier`). Add OID dispatch for the two new OIDs in `DefaultVerifier`.

The `sha2` workspace dep already provides `Sha384` and `Sha512`; the `rsa` crate already supports both. No new deps needed.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Both algorithms have working verifiers.
- [ ] Unit tests using NIST CAVS or RustCrypto rsa-crate test vectors (independent oracle).
- [ ] Tampered-signature test for each.
- [ ] `DefaultVerifier` dispatches both.
- [ ] No new top-level deps.

## Filed as

PKIX-gphz child #4. Lower priority — most CAs use SHA-256 today; SHA-384/512 RSA is rarer.
